sentences.text:
Mamidipally Saravva And 3 Others vs Mugala Ajay Kumar And 3
Others on 10 January, 2025
 The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.460 Of 2013
 And
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1324 Of 2019
Common Judgment

entities.text: Mamidipally Saravva And 3 Others vs Mugala Ajay Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
:
1. These two appeals are being disposed of by this common judgment since M.A.C.M.A.No.460 of 2013 filed by the respondent No.2 in O.P./Driver of the offending car seeking to set-aside the Award passed by the Tribunal and M.A.C.M.A.No.1324 of 2019 filed by the claim petitioners to enhance the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal; both are directed against the very same order and decree dated 28.09.2012 passed in O.P.No.215 of 2010 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- District Judge, Karimnagar (for short, "the Tribunal").
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in the Appeal are referred as they were arrayed before the learned Tribunal.

3. The facts of the case in nutshell are that the petitioners, who are the wife, son and daughters of one Mamidipally Kanakaiah (hereinafter be referred as "the deceased"), filed a claim petition under Section 166 (1)(c) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- along with interest @ 18% per annum for the death the deceased in a motor vehicle accident that MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 occurred on 04.03.2009 at about 19.00 hours.

It is stated by the petitioners that on 04.03.2009, when the deceased-Kanakaiah along with his wife went to Eedulagattepalli Village for attending their relative's marriage and when the deceased alone was returning to Porandla Village on his TVS Moped bearing No.AP-15- AH-6477, on the way at about 7.00 P.M., when he reached the bridge situated at the outskirts of Eedulagattepalli Village, the respondent No.1, who was the driver of Car bearing No.AP-13W- 7022, drove the said car in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and dashed against the deceased, due to which he fell down and received severe bleeding injuries to his both legs and also Head and his Moped also damaged.

Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Apollo Hospoital, Karimnagar and after taking First Aid, he was again shifted to Devishetty Super Speciality Hospital, Karimnagar and while undergoing treatment, he died on 11.03.2009.

4. Based on a complaint, Police of Manakondur Police Station, registered a case in Crime No.37 of 2009 under Section 337 IPC, conducted investigation and filed charge sheet against respondent No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 304-A IPC.
5.

It is stated by the petitioner that the deceased was aged 42 years and was hale and healthy and used to work as Hamali in Sai MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 Parboiled Rice Mill, Ramakrishnapur Colony of Thimmapur Mandal and used to earn Rs.6,000/- to Rs.7,000/- per Mamidipally Saravva And 3 Others vs Mugala Ajay Kumar And 3 Others on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172536972/
1 month and maintain his family.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Due to the untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners have lost their source of income and were suffering with mental shock and agony and therefore, filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- from the respondent Nos.1 to 4 jointly and severally.
6. Before the Tribunal, respondent No.3 remained ex-parte and Respondent Nos.1, 2 & 4 filed their respective counters.

Though Respondent Nos.1 & 2/Driver and owner of offending Car bearing No.AP-13W-7022 filed separate counters, but they took the pleas akin to each other and contended that the petitioners, in collusion with Police, falsely implicated respondent No.1 in the accident.

They also denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased and also denied the manner of accident as narrated by the petitioners in the claim petition and further contended that as the offending car had been insured with respondent No.4 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident, hence, respondent No.4 alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

7. Respondent No.4/Insurance Company filed its counter denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation and income of the deceased and contended that MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 respondent No.1 was not having any valid driving license to drive the offending car and the said crime vehicle Car was not insured with Insurance Company and further contended that the owner of the offending vehicle had not informed the Insurance Company about the accident and that FIR was also not received by them under Section 158(6) of M.V.Act and hence, they are not liable to pay compensation and prayed to dismiss the claim against it.

8. Based on the pleadings made by both the parties, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues:-
(i) Whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car Bearing No.AP- 13-W-7022?

(ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
(iii) To what relief?
9.

Before the Tribunal, petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased examined herself as PW1 and got examined PW2, an eye witness to the incident and also PW3-Baddam Venkat Reddy, employer of the deceased and got marked Exs.A1 to A9 on behalf of petitioners.
On behalf of Respondent No.4/Insurance Company, RWs1 & 2 were examined and Exs.B1 to B3 were marked.
MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 10.

After considering the entire oral and documentary evidence available on record, the learned Tribunal had awarded an amount of Rs.3,91,000/- towards compensation along with interest @
Mamidipally Saravva And 3 Others vs Mugala Ajay Kumar And 3 Others on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172536972/
2 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit payable by Respondent Nos.1 & 2 alone jointly and severally and exempted the Insurance Company from its liability in paying compensation.

entities.text: Mamidipally Saravva And 3 Others vs Mugala Ajay Kumar And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Challenging the said Award, the present appeals came to be filed by respondent No.2/Owner of offending crime vehicle and the claimants respectively.

11. Heard Sri K.M.Mahender Reddy, learned counsel for the appellants/claim petitioners, Sri L.Srihar, learned counsel for respondent No.1/Driver of offending Car in M.A.C.M.A.No.1324 of 2019 and Sri K.Ramchandra Reddy, learned counsel for appellant/Owner of offending Car in M.A.C.M.A.No.460 of 2013.
Perused the material available on record.

12. The contentions raised by the learned counsel for appellant/owner of crime vehicle in M.A.C.M.A.No.460 of 2013 as stated in the grounds of Appeal are that the learned Tribunal had grossly erred in exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability and also failed to consider the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case between MUKUND DEWANGAN Vs. MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED 1 wherein, it is held that a driver who is holding valid driving license to drive non-transport LMV vehicle is also authorized to drive LMV transport vehicle 13.

entities.text: MUKUND DEWANGAN Vs. MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, the contentions of the learned counsel for appellants/claim petitioners in M.A.C.M.A.No.1324 of 2019 are that the learned Tribunal failed to consider income of the deceased in a proper perspective and also erred in exempting the Insurance Company from its liability in paying compensation and therefore requested to allow the Appeal by enhancing the compensation amount.

14. Now the points that emerges for determination are,
(i). Whether the order passed by the learned Tribunal suffers from any irregularity?
(ii). Whether the appellants in M.A.C.M.A.No.1324 of 2019 are entitled for enhancement of compensation? POINTS:-
15.
There is no dispute about the occurrence of accident and death of the deceased as evident from the oral and documentary evidence filed under Exs.A1 to A9.

A perusal of Ex.A1 shows that Police of Manakondur Police Station registered a case in Crime No.37 of 2009 under Section 337 IPC,
conducted investigation and filed charge sheet under Ex.A4 against respondent No.1 for the (2017)
14 Supreme Court Cases 663 MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 offence punishable under Section 304-A IPC.

entities.text: Supreme Court Cases 663 MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ex.A2 is the Inquest Report.
Ex.A3 is the Post-mortem examination report wherein the cause of death is shown as shock, Haemorrhage i.e., polytrauma and Head injury.
Ex.A5 is Form-54.
Ex.A6 is the report of Motor Vehicle Inspector which shows that the accident had not occurred due to any mechanical defect in the vehicle.
Ex.A7 is the extract of Employees Provident Fund Register for the year 2006-07.
Exs. A8
& A9 are the Debit Vouchers.
Further the evidence of PW2, an eye witness to the incident also shows that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Driver of offending Car.

Mamidipally Saravva And 3 Others vs Mugala Ajay Kumar And 3 Others on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172536972/
3 16.

entities.text: Mamidipally Saravva And 3 Others vs Mugala Ajay Kumar And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, from the above oral and documentary evidence, it is clear that the death of the deceased was due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car which finding of the Tribunal attains finality and needs no interference by this Court.
17. The Only points that have to be dealt with in the present Appeal are with regard to quantum of compensation and imposing of liability.

18. Coming to the aspect of compensation, though the learned counsel for petitioners stated that the deceased used to earn Rs.6,000/- to Rs.7,000/- per month by working as a 'Hamali', they did not file any documentary proof in support of their contention.
Hence, the learned Tribunal, in the absence of documentary proof, MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 fixed the income of the deceased @ Rs.3,000/- per month.

This Court finds the said amount to be meager and is inclined to interfere with the same by relying upon the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Latha Wadhwa vs. State of Bihar 2, wherein it is held that even though there is no proof of income and earnings, the income can be reasonably estimated by considering the age, avocation and year of accident, and hereby fix the monthly income @ Rs.4,500/- and calculate the compensation as under.

entities.text: Latha Wadhwa vs. State of Bihar 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking into account Ex.B3-Household card, considered the age of the deceased as 48 years on the date of accident and upon addition of 25% towards future prospects as the deceased being self- employed and by relying upon decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 3, arrived at a total income of Rs.5,625/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the number of dependents are four, if 1/4th is deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased,
then the net monthly income of the deceased would be Rs.4,219/-.

After application of relevant multiplier 13 as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 4 , then the total loss of dependency works out to Rs.6,58,164/- (Rs.4,219/x12x 13).

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. That apart, the learned Tribunal had also awarded an (2001) 8 SCC 197 2017 ACJ 2700 2009 ACJ 1298 (SC) MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 amount of Rs.40,000/- under the head of non-pecuniary damages which this Court finds it to be meager and is inclined to interfere with the same by relying upon the Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.Pranay Sethi & others (2017 ACJ 2700) and hereby grant an amount of Rs.77,000/- towards conventional heads i.e. loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.Pranay Sethi & others (2017 ACJ 2700)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus in all, the appellants are entitled for a total compensation which is calculated as under:-
 S.No. Name of the Head Awarded by Awarded by  the Tribunal this Court.
 1. Monthly income of Rs.3,000 Rs.4,500/-
 the deceased  2. Amount arrived after - Rs.5,625/-
 addition of future  prospects  3. Deduction of 1/4th Rs.9,000/- Rs.50,628/-
 towards personal  and living expenses  of the deceased Mamidipally Saravva And 3 Others vs Mugala Ajay Kumar And 3 Others on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172536972/
4  3. Loss of dependency Rs.3,51,000/- Rs.6,58,164 /-
4 . Conventional heads Rs.40,000/- Rs.77,000/-

5. TOTAL Rs.3,91,000/- Rs.7,35,164/-
 COMPENSATION 20.

Coming to the aspect of liability, the learned Tribunal taking into consideration the evidence of RW2-Administrative Officer in Road Transport Authority, Karimnagar, who deposed in his MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 evidence that the driver of the offending car (respondent No.1) cannot drive transport vehicle as he was holding driving license to drive LMV(non-transport) vehicle and Ex.B2-Driving license of respondent No.1, wherein it is mentioned that respondent No.1 was authorized to drive motorcycle with gear (non-transport) and light motor vehicle (Non-transport), exempted Insurance Company from its liability in paying compensation amount and imposed liability upon respondent Nos.1 & 2 only as they pleaded in their counters that respondent No.3, who is also alleged to be owner of the offending car, is no way concerned with the said crime vehicle.
Further, Ex.A6-MVI report also shows the name of respondent No.2 as owner of the offending car and not respondent No.3.

Hence, the Tribunal exempted respondent No.3.
21.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for appellant/owner of crime vehicle in M.A.C.M.A.No.460 of 2013 as well as learned counsel for claim petitioners/appellants in M.A.C.M.A.No.1324 of 2019 that the learned Tribunal had grossly erred in exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability and failed to consider the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case between MUKUND DEWANGAN Vs. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED 5.
(2017) 14 Supreme Court Cases 663 MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 22.

entities.text: MUKUND DEWANGAN Vs. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
5.
(2017) 14 Supreme Court Cases 663 MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A perusal of the Para No.59 of the above judgment discloses that light motor vehicle includes transport vehicle and a holder of light motor vehicle license can drive all the vehicles of the class including transport vehicles.
23.

In the instant case, as the driver of the offending Car bearing No.AP-13W-7022 is holding valid driving license to drive LMV (non- transport) vehicle as per Ex.B2-Driving license and as the Insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident, this Court, by relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court (cited supra) deems fit and proper to include the Insurance Company in making liable to pay the compensation amount along with the other respondents, who are the owner and driver of offending Car bearing No.AP-13W-7022.
24.

In the result, MACMA.460 of 2013 is allowed by making the Insurance Company liable to pay the compensation along with other respondents and M.A.C.M.A.1324 of 2019 is partly-allowed by enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.3,91,000/- to Rs.7,35,164/-
which shall carry interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by respondent Nos.1, 2 & 4 in O.P. viz., the driver, owner and Insurance Company jointly and severally within a period of MGP,J MACMA.Nos.460 of 2013 and 1324 of 2019 two months from the date of Mamidipally Saravva And 3 Others vs Mugala Ajay Kumar And 3 Others on 10 January, 2025

5 receipt of a copy of this order.
Upon such deposit, the claimants are entitled to withdraw the same as per the apportionment made by the learned Tribunal.
There shall be no order as to costs.
25. Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
